title: Zion Stands with Hills Surrounded
description: Zion Stands with Hills Surrounded in Tonic Solfa to ST. AUSTIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Kelly wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 465.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked 8.7.8.7.4.7, to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AUSTIN; any other 8.7.8.7.4.7 tune fits them as well.
underlay: Zi-on stands with hills sur-round-ed, Zi-on, kept by power di-vine; All her foes shall be con-found-ed, Though the world in arms com-bine. Hap-py Zi-on, What a hap-py lot is thine!

lines: All her foes shall be confounded,
Though the world in arms combine.
What a happy lot is thine!
Brothers cease their own to cherish,
Heaven and earth at last remove;
In the furnace God may prove thee,
Thence to bring thee forth more bright,
But can never cease to love thee;
Thou art precious in His sight;

licence: Public domain: Thomas Kelly died in 1855.
credits: Words by Thomas Kelly (1769–1855), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. AUSTIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
